agree.reason: The 74-household, two-in-three figure undercuts her view that this is a few loud people, and the measured tone and low-cost first two asks give her an easy way to say yes, though she may still feel the outages were handled fine.

honest.reason: Every number traces to the brief, but 'some of them cannot get down to the street at all' and the specific claim 'It is now November' go slightly beyond what the brief states.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the counts into 'one day in every eight' and 'two out of every three apartments', but it never says that the June estimate of six to eight weeks ran out in August, which would be the sharpest fact against management.

right_comparison.reason: It describes doing nothing as another twelve-day outage landing on the same frail residents, and it shows the pattern of repeated estimates, though it gives no outage trend beyond that.

qualification.reason: The 'If that is so, please show us why' hedge points to a checkable engineering assessment, and there is a two-week reply deadline, but the letter never says what happens if management misses it.

objections.reason: It deals with the passing certificate and the $400,000 cost before she can raise them, and it does not bring up objections the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It is a proper open letter of roughly 430 words, fit to post in the lobby, with clear numbered requests and a signature line.
